Education | U.S. Congressman Steve Womack <span style="font-size: 18px;">The education of our nation’s children is the foundation for our success.&nbsp; While I agree that we must make sure our teachers have the tools to adequately provide quality education, we need to make sure they are not burdened by disconnected bureaucratic mandates.&nbsp; Our federal policies should offer limited standards for schools, not detailed policy directives.&nbsp; Basic education policies are best decided by those in our local communities.</span></p> <p><span style="font-size: 18px;">During my three terms as mayor of Rogers, I saw firsthand how our communities are challenged to adequately prepare our students for their futures.&nbsp; By handing down one-size-fits-all directives, we reduce the ability of our kids to think critically and solve the problems our nation is facing.&nbsp; As your representative in Congress, I will work to strike the balance between federal involvement and local control to ensure our children are receiving the best possible education.</span></p>" /> Skip to Content Education Share on Facebook Share on Twitter Print this Page Share by Email The education of our nation’s children is the foundation for our success.  While I agree that we must make sure our teachers have the tools to adequately provide quality education, we need to make sure they are not burdened by disconnected bureaucratic mandates.  Our federal policies should offer limited standards for schools, not detailed policy directives.  Basic education policies are best decided by those in our local communities. During my three terms as mayor of Rogers, I saw firsthand how our communities are challenged to adequately prepare our students for their futures.  By handing down one-size-fits-all directives, we reduce the ability of our kids to think critically and solve the problems our nation is facing.  As your representative in Congress, I will work to strike the balance between federal involvement and local control to ensure our children are receiving the best possible education. Energy | U.S. Congressman Steve Womack <span style="font-size: 18px;">Domestic energy production is essential to the growth of our economy and to the security of our nation.&nbsp; We must take an all-of-the-above approach to our energy policy and allow all American energy sources – oil, gas, coal, nuclear, and renewables – to compete on a level playing field.&nbsp; While I support research and development of new energy technologies, I do not believe the government should be in the business of picking winners and losers.</span></p> <p><span style="font-size: 18px;">The production of affordable American energy supplies is driving job creation and fueling the growth of other major sectors of economy. I will continue to support policies to remove barriers to domestic energy production and stop harmful regulations from driving up energy costs. With the right policies in place, I believe we can achieve the goal of American energy independence.</span></p>" /> Skip to Content Energy Share on Facebook Share on Twitter Print this Page Share by Email Domestic energy production is essential to the growth of our economy and to the security of our nation.  We must take an all-of-the-above approach to our energy policy and allow all American energy sources – oil, gas, coal, nuclear, and renewables – to compete on a level playing field.  While I support research and development of new energy technologies, I do not believe the government should be in the business of picking winners and losers. The production of affordable American energy supplies is driving job creation and fueling the growth of other major sectors of economy. I will continue to support policies to remove barriers to domestic energy production and stop harmful regulations from driving up energy costs. With the right policies in place, I believe we can achieve the goal of American energy independence. Immigration | U.S. Congressman Steve Womack <span style="font-size: 18px;"></span></p> <p><span style="font-size: 18px;">Illegal immigration continues to be a serious problem in Arkansas and across our country. &nbsp;Our system is broken, and now is the time for Congress to act.&nbsp; Any solution must secure our border and encourage lawful behavior.&nbsp;</span></p> <p><span style="font-size: 18px;">Over the past couple of years, we have only seen the issue worsen as evidenced by sanctuary cities deliberately disregarding the rule of law. I continue to believe that we must secure the border and develop a long-term immigration policy that encourages lawful behavior.</span></p> <p><span style="font-size: 18px;">I will continue to support programs like Section 287(G) of the Illegal Immigration Reform and Immigrant Responsibility Act which allows police officers to receive specialized training from U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents.&nbsp; As the mayor of Rogers, I saw firsthand how valuable this tool was in ensuring the safety of citizens in the community.</span></p>" /> Skip to Content Immigration Share on Facebook Share on Twitter Print this Page Share by Email Illegal immigration continues to be a serious problem in Arkansas and across our country.  Our system is broken, and now is the time for Congress to act.  Any solution must secure our border and encourage lawful behavior.  Over the past couple of years, we have only seen the issue worsen as evidenced by sanctuary cities deliberately disregarding the rule of law. I continue to believe that we must secure the border and develop a long-term immigration policy that encourages lawful behavior. I will continue to support programs like Section 287(G) of the Illegal Immigration Reform and Immigrant Responsibility Act which allows police officers to receive specialized training from U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents.  As the mayor of Rogers, I saw firsthand how valuable this tool was in ensuring the safety of citizens in the community.
